entry.title: SETI Rules: From Setup to Your First Complete Game

link.title: SETI Rules: From Setup to Your First Complete Game

entry.content:
1. Scope and How to Use This Guide

This guide teaches the complete base game first. It then covers Space Agencies and all four official promo cards. Expansion rules are kept out of the base-game procedure.

For a first game, read in order and set out the components as you go. Experienced players may skip directly to the expansion section. Detailed rules for the three new alien species are hidden in a spoiler disclosure.

Eight short “Further Context” boxes focus on how separate rules join into action chains. External knowledge is limited to one useful layer. These boxes add no rulings; official text and card wording always control.

Rules references

  • Base game: official Simplified Chinese rulebook and official FAQ.
  • Expansion: official Simplified Chinese Space Agencies rulebook and alien-species aid.
  • Promo cards: official promo-card rules.
  • Individual card cases: continuously updated official card-clarification thread.

2. Objective and Table Overview

The base game lasts 5 rounds. The player with the most points after final scoring wins. Tied players share the victory.

The main sources of points are:

  • project cards and endgame cards with gold text boxes;
  • technologies;
  • sector victories;
  • missions and milestones;
  • landings, alien discoveries, and further research.

Figure: A complete game at a glance. Official SETI media assets, © Czech Games Edition; this site only resizes and compresses the image and adds a neutral background.

The table has four main areas:

  1. Central Solar System: probes leave Earth and move among the planets.
  2. Eight nearby-star sectors: players mark signals, collect data, and compete for majorities.
  3. Planet, technology, and alien-species boards: these handle landings, upgrades, and alien traces.
  4. Player areas: these hold credits, energy, cards, probes, data, and technologies.

There are three types of alien trace:

  • pink: gained mainly from scanning and winning sectors;
  • yellow: gained mainly from landing on planets;
  • blue: gained mainly from analyzing data.

A wild trace shows all three colors. Choose pink, yellow, or blue when you gain it.

Further Context — Biosignatures and technosignatures

NASA calls observable evidence left by life biosignatures and evidence left by technology technosignatures. The game groups traces by action source: scanning and sectors connect to pink, landing to yellow, and analysis to blue. This color system links rules; it does not model scientific evidence categories.

3. Three-Player Setup

Shared Area

  1. Assemble the planet, Solar System, and technology boards.
  2. Shuffle the 5 alien-species boards. Place 2 at random, face down. Return the other 3 to the box without looking at them.
  3. Leave all species-specific cards, rule sheets, and components in the box. Take out a set only when that species is revealed.
  4. Randomly combine the three Solar System discs and 4 sector boards to form 8 clearly bounded sectors. Each sector has one nearby star.
  5. Fill each star’s printed data slot to its shown capacity. The stars do not all hold the same amount. Keep the remaining data, credits, and energy beside the board as shared supplies.
  6. Shuffle the main deck and reveal 3 cards to form the card row.
  7. Randomly choose one side of each of the 4 gold milestone tiles.
  8. Choose an unused player color for neutral markers. Place 1 neutral marker at both 20 and 30 points.
  9. For each of the 12 technologies, shuffle its 4 tiles into a face-down stack. Place a “first research +2 points” marker on each stack.
  10. Prepare one end-of-round stack for rounds 1–4. Each three-player stack contains 4 cards: the player count plus one.
  11. Put one rotation reminder on the technology board’s rotation track and the other on the round 1 stack.

Player Areas

Each player:

  1. Chooses a color and takes its player board, starting-income card, 8 probes, 30 markers, score counter, and publicity counter.
  2. Starts on 1, 2, or 3 points in turn order. The player who most recently saw a UFO takes the starting-player marker.
  3. Sets publicity to 4, takes 4 credits and 3 energy, and draws 5 cards.
  4. Tucks 1 hand card under the starting-income card and immediately gains the credit, energy, or card reward in its lower-right corner.

Tucking a credit- or energy-income card leaves 4 cards in hand. Tucking a card-income card immediately draws a replacement, leaving 5 cards.

Figure: A player area contains three technology rows, the data pool, the computer, income, and resource tracks. Official SETI media assets, © Czech Games Edition; this site only resizes and compresses the image and adds a neutral background.

Other Player Counts

Players Neutral markers at 20 and 30 Cards in each round stack
2 2 at each threshold 3
3 1 at each threshold 4
4 None 5

4. Turn Structure and Free Actions

During a round, players repeatedly take turns in order. A player who has passed takes no more turns that round. The others continue until everyone has passed.

A turn follows this structure:

  1. Take any desired free actions before the main action.
  2. Choose and complete 1 main action; free actions may also interrupt it.
  3. When the main action ends, immediately resolve every sector completed by it. The active player chooses the order if several sectors completed.
  4. Free actions may still be taken after sector resolution.
  5. End the turn: resolve milestones first, then alien discoveries.

Figure: The seven main actions and Pass. Official Simplified Chinese rulebook, page 7, © Czech Games Edition; this site only makes the necessary local crop.

Main action Base cost and requirement
Launch a probe 2 credits; place it on Earth
Orbit a planet 1 credit + 1 energy; a probe has reached that planet
Land on a planet or moon Usually 3 energy; a probe has reached the target
Scan nearby stars 1 credit + 2 energy
Analyze data 1 energy; all 6 upper computer spaces are filled
Play a card Pay the cost in its white effect area
Research a technology 6 publicity; you do not own that technology
Pass No cost; take no more turns this round

Common free actions:

  • spend 1 energy to move one probe 1 space;
  • discard 1 hand card to use its upper-left effect;
  • move 1 data from the data pool into the computer;
  • pay two resources of one kind to gain 1 credit, 1 energy, or 1 card;
  • spend 3 publicity to buy 1 card from the card row or the top of the deck;
  • complete a card mission whose condition is currently satisfied;
  • use a free action printed on a component.

A resource exchange can use 2 cards, 2 credits, or 2 energy. Types cannot be mixed. Each data placement and each space of probe movement is a separate free action.

Free actions can be used only on your own turn. A free action may interrupt a main action, but one free action cannot interrupt another. Triggered missions are among the few effects that can respond during another player’s turn.

Effects are mandatory unless stated otherwise. Only movement and income increases may be declined. Rotations, signals, technologies, resources, points, alien traces, card-granted main actions, and milestones cannot be skipped. If one part of an effect is impossible, skip only that part.

5. Probe Actions

Figure: The same miniature can be a probe, orbiter, or lander; its location defines its role. Official SETI media assets, © Czech Games Edition; this site only resizes and compresses the image.

Launch and Move

Launch costs 2 credits. Place 1 probe from your supply on Earth. By default, you may have only 1 probe in space.

The new probe may move during the same turn. Spend 1 energy for each orthogonally adjacent space:

  • movement is never diagonal;
  • the Sun cannot be entered or crossed;
  • leaving an asteroid costs 1 extra movement; entering it does not;
  • entering a celestial body with a publicity icon gains 1 publicity; Earth is excluded;
  • visiting the same body again can gain its publicity again.

A probe may remain in space and move, orbit, or land on a later turn.

Orbit

After a probe reaches a planet other than Earth, a later turn may use the Orbit action:

  1. Pay 1 credit and 1 energy.
  2. Move the miniature from the Solar System to that planet’s orbit.
  3. Gain the orbit reward. The first player to orbit that planet also scores 3 points.

An orbiter no longer moves and cannot later become a lander. It does not count against the limit of probes in space.

Land

After a probe reaches its target, a later turn may use the Land action:

  1. Pay 3 energy in most cases.
  2. If any player already has an orbiter at that planet, the cost is 2 energy.
  3. Move the miniature to the landing area and gain its points, printed reward, and yellow trace.
  4. The first lander usually gains data as well.

Mars has two data spaces, so its first two landers each gain data.

Landing on a moon requires the matching probe technology or explicit permission from an effect. Gain only the reward printed on the moon space. A yellow trace is gained only if that space shows one. Each moon space holds 1 lander.

A lander no longer moves and does not count against the limit of probes in space.

Further Context — The probe mission chain

A complete chain is usually launch → free movement → orbit or land on a later turn. A launch may come from a main action or card; movement may come from energy or cards; technologies and existing orbiters can change routes and costs. When reading a card effect, identify which step it replaces, then supply the remaining position and cost requirements.

6. Scanning and Sector Resolution

Scan

Scan costs 1 credit and 2 energy. A basic scan must mark two signals; complete the following two steps in either order:

  1. Mark 1 signal in the sector currently aligned with Earth.
  2. Discard 1 card from the card row. Choose one of the two sector colors in its upper-right corner and mark 1 signal in a matching sector.

Refill the card row only after the entire scan and all technology effects are complete. Telescope technologies may move or add signals. A scan can mark up to 4 signals, and any extra technology costs must still be paid.

Figure: The two signals of a basic scan and the telescope technologies. Official Simplified Chinese rulebook, page 12, © Czech Games Edition; this site only makes the necessary local crop.

Mark a Signal

Each time you mark a signal:

  1. Take the leftmost data token from that sector and put it in your data pool.
  2. Replace the token with one of your player markers.
  3. If you fill the second space, immediately score 2 points.

Marking a signal is mandatory. If every data space already contains a marker, place an excess signal beside that slot. It gains no data but counts in the upcoming majority comparison.

Resolve a Sector

Replacing the final data token completes the sector. Resolve it when the current main action ends:

  1. The player with the most markers wins. Ties go to the marker placed later.
  2. The winner places a record marker beside the nearby star and gains its reward.
  3. Every player who contributed at least 1 signal gains 1 publicity, including the winner.
  4. Determine second place using the same count and tiebreaker. If there is one, that player leaves 1 marker in the first space after reset.
  5. Return all other markers and refill the empty spaces with data.

Excess signals count for the majority and participation; each player still gains only 1 publicity per resolution. Earlier victory markers beside the star do not count in the next contest. A sector can be completed and won repeatedly.

Figure: Sector majority, rewards, the second-place marker, and reset. Official Simplified Chinese rulebook, page 13, © Czech Games Edition; this site only makes the necessary local crop.

Sector resolution occurs when the main action ends. To place data, buy a card, or complete a mission before resolution, insert those free actions during the main action.

7. Data and Analysis

New data enters the data pool. Its capacity is 6; excess data must be discarded.

On your turn, a free action moves 1 data from the pool into the computer:

  • the 6 upper spaces of the base computer fill from left to right;
  • gain any publicity, income increase, or points shown on a covered space immediately;
  • computer technologies add one upper and one lower space;
  • a lower space can be filled only after its upper space is occupied;
  • lower spaces do not have to be filled from left to right.

When all 6 base upper spaces are filled, Analyze Data costs 1 energy:

  1. Clear all data from the upper and lower computer spaces.
  2. Keep all data still in the data pool.
  3. Mark 1 blue alien trace.

Technology spaces below the base row may remain empty.

Figure: Data moves from the pool to the computer; analysis requires a full upper row. Official Simplified Chinese rulebook, page 14, © Czech Games Edition; this site only makes the necessary local crop.

Further Context — From candidate signal to evidence chain

Real SETI rejects interference and repeats candidate observations; Project Phoenix also used a second telescope for confirmation. The game’s main chain is scan → signal → data pool → computer → analysis → blue trace. If a scan fills a sector, finish the scan and any free actions inserted into it, then resolve the sector when the main action ends; when the pool nears 6, first check whether you can load or analyze data.

8. Four Uses for a Card

A hand card can be used in one of four ways:

  1. Play it: use a main action, pay the cost in the white area, and resolve the effect.
  2. Discard it: use a free action and resolve the upper-left effect.
  3. Increase income: when allowed by an effect, tuck it under the starting-income card. Gain its lower-right reward immediately and again during later income phases.
  4. Exchange resources: pay it together with another hand card to gain 1 credit, 1 energy, or 1 card.

Further Context — Opportunity cost

Opportunity cost is the best alternative forgone when one use is chosen. A card can enter four chains: its main effect, its discard free action, long-term income, or a two-card resource exchange. If its main effect grants another action, that action skips its base cost but keeps position requirements, technology surcharges, and any resulting mission, sector, and trace resolution.

Figure: Physical project cards. Official SETI media assets, © Czech Games Edition; this site only resizes and compresses the image.

Figure: The upper-left free action, lower-left cost, white effect, upper-right sector colors, and lower-right income. Official Simplified Chinese rulebook, page 7, © Czech Games Edition; this site only makes the necessary local crop.

If a card directly grants a launch, scan, orbit, landing, analysis, or research action, do not pay that action’s base cost. All position and legality requirements still apply. Extra costs on technologies must still be paid when those technologies are used.

There are two mission types:

  • Conditional mission: complete it as a free action on any of your turns while its condition is still true.
  • Triggered mission: it records only events that happen after the card is played. You may decline one trigger, but a qualifying event must happen again before you can mark it.

One event can mark only 1 reward circle on the same mission. Cards with gold text boxes are endgame cards; keep them after playing them and score them at the end of the game.

When a card leaves the card row, refill it to 3 immediately. Scanning is the exception: refill only after the scan. If the main deck runs out, shuffle the discard pile into a new deck.

9. Technology and Solar System Rotation

Publicity has a maximum of 10. With at least 6 publicity, research one technology you do not own:

  1. Spend 6 publicity.
  2. Rotate the Solar System first.
  3. Take the top tile from the matching technology stack.
  4. If this is the first tile taken from that stack, remove its “first research +2 points” marker and score 2 points.
  5. Gain the one-time reward on the tile’s face, then flip and install it on your player board.

Figure: Probe, telescope, and computer technologies. Official SETI media assets, © Czech Games Edition; this site only resizes and compresses the image.

  • Probe technologies: raise the in-space probe limit, improve asteroid movement, reduce landing costs, or unlock moons.
  • Telescope technologies: operate only during scans and move or add signals.
  • Computer technologies: add data spaces; the upper space usually scores 2 points and the lower space gives another reward.

Solar System rotation follows a fixed cycle:

  1. The first rotation turns only the top disc.
  2. The second turns the middle disc and carries the top disc.
  3. The third turns the bottom disc and carries both discs above it.
  4. The fourth returns to the top disc.

Every affected disc turns one sector counterclockwise.

Figure: The 1→2→3 Solar System rotation cycle. Official Simplified Chinese rulebook, page 16, © Czech Games Edition; this site only makes the necessary local crop.

Further Context — Orbital mechanics and a discrete model

Kepler’s third law says that more distant orbits generally take longer; the game retains only changing relative positions through its 1→2→3 disc cycle. The research chain is spend publicity → rotate → resolve moved or pushed probes → take the technology → gain its reward, so the new technology cannot affect that rotation. The first player to pass triggers the same rotation and changes routes and Earth’s aligned sector for players still active.

Rotation is triggered when:

  • a player gains a technology through a main action or card;
  • the first player passes in each round.

The first player to pass in round 5 still rotates the system. A rotation icon printed beside a technology icon on a card is a reminder, not a second rotation.

Open spaces between the incomplete discs are gaps. Resolve each probe from its current position:

  • A probe on a rotating disc moves one sector with that disc.
  • A probe in a gap remains where it is if the disc does not touch it.
  • If a rotating disc reaches a probe in a gap, push that probe into the next space.

A probe pushed onto a celestial body with a publicity icon gains that publicity, even during another player’s turn.

10. Passing and the End of a Round

Pass is a main action. You may take free actions first, then resolve:

  1. If you have more than 4 cards, discard down to 4. There is no hand limit at other times.
  2. If you are the first player to pass this round, rotate the Solar System.
  3. In rounds 1–4, choose 1 remaining card from the round’s end-of-round stack and add it to your hand.

In a three-player game, the first player chooses from 4 cards, the second from 3, and the last from 2. The final unchosen card is discarded.

After passing, you take no more turns or free actions that round.

Figure: Discard to 4, rotate for the first pass, and choose an end-of-round card. Official Simplified Chinese rulebook, page 19, © Czech Games Edition; this site only makes the necessary local crop.

After everyone passes in rounds 1–4:

  1. Each player gains 3 credits, 2 energy, and 1 card from the starting-income card.
  2. Each player gains all tucked income.
  3. Pass the starting-player marker clockwise.
  4. Move the rotation reminder to the next round stack.

Credits, energy, and cards carry over between rounds. Round 5 has no end-of-round cards. When the final player passes, proceed directly to final scoring and do not collect income.

Further Context — Pass links two rounds

The chain is finish final free actions → discard to 4 → first passer rotates → in rounds 1–4 choose an end-of-round card → wait for everyone to pass → collect income; after round 5, proceed directly to final scoring. The first passer changes the Solar System before the others finish the round. Passing ends access to free actions, so resolve any eligible card missions, data loading, and resource exchanges first.

11. Alien Traces, Milestones, and Discovery

Here, “milestones” means the gold milestone tiles beside the board. Card missions are resolved separately.

Place an Alien Trace

When you gain an alien trace, you must place a marker in a matching-color location. Before a species is revealed, choose:

  • Discovery space: place the marker in an empty matching space beneath either species; gain 1 publicity and 5 points.
  • Overflow area: place it in a matching area for either species; score 3 points.

Each species has one pink, yellow, and blue overflow area. These areas never fill; markers of the same color may accumulate. You may choose overflow even while a discovery space remains empty.

Figure: The three trace types, discovery spaces, and alien reveal procedure. Official Simplified Chinese rulebook, page 20, © Czech Games Edition; this site only makes the necessary local crop.

End-of-Turn Milestones

The first time you reach or pass 25, 50, or 70 points, choose a gold milestone you have not selected before. Place your marker on its highest open scoring position. If one turn crosses several thresholds, resolve each one. The milestone scores only at the end of the game.

In a three-player game, a neutral marker waits at both 20 and 30 points. The first player to reach or pass a threshold moves that marker to the leftmost empty discovery space among all six: fill the three spaces under the left species first, then the right. Neutral markers never enter overflow or a revealed species board, but they can complete a discovery.

If several players reach milestones during one turn, resolve them clockwise from the active player. Place all neutral markers before checking for alien discovery.

Reveal an Alien Species

When all three discovery spaces beneath one species are filled, reveal it after the current turn:

  1. Resolve every milestone first.
  2. Flip the species board.
  3. Take out that species’ rules sheet, cards, and components.
  4. Follow its setup instructions.
  5. Each player occupying a discovery space gains the reward printed for discovery on that space. Do not repeat the 5 points and 1 publicity already gained when the marker was placed.

Markers in overflow do not receive the discovery-contribution reward.

After a species is revealed, a new alien trace may be placed in:

  • an empty matching space on a revealed species board;
  • an empty matching discovery space beneath a hidden species;
  • a matching overflow area for either species.

Spaces on a revealed species board do not fill from bottom to top. Gain the reward printed on the space you choose.

Further Context — Alien discovery joins several action chains

Scanning and sectors, landing, and analysis produce pink, yellow, and blue markers; each can be placed in the shared discovery structure. A neutral milestone marker can also fill a space when a score threshold is crossed, so an action that only scores points may still cause a discovery at turn end. Before ending a turn, check score thresholds, discovery spaces, and their resolution order together.

12. A Complete Three-Player First Round

This example uses only guaranteed starting resources. It does not rely on random planet or sector rewards.

Assumptions:

  • A, B, and C act in that order and start on 1, 2, and 3 points.
  • Venus is orthogonally adjacent to Earth, with no asteroid exit between them.
  • A and C tuck credit-income cards. B tucks an energy-income card.
  • After setup, A and C each have 5 credits and 3 energy. B has 4 credits and 4 energy. Everyone has 4 cards and 4 publicity.
  • No scan in this example completes a sector.

Action Log

  1. A launches and moves. A pays 2 credits and places a probe on Earth, then uses a free action to spend 1 energy and move to Venus. Visiting Venus gains 1 publicity. A has 3 credits and 2 energy left.
  2. B scans. B pays 1 credit and 2 energy, marks Earth’s sector, then discards a row card and marks the second sector. The row refills after the scan. Assume both signals gain data. B uses two free actions to fill computer spaces 1 and 2 and gains the publicity on space 2. B has 3 credits and 2 energy left.
  3. C launches and moves. C follows the same procedure as A and has 3 credits and 2 energy left.
  4. A orbits Venus. A pays 1 credit and 1 energy, moves the probe to Venus’s orbit, gains the orbit reward, and scores 3 points for being first.
  5. B passes. B discards down to 4 cards if necessary, rotates the Solar System as the first player to pass, and chooses 1 of the 4 end-of-round cards.
  6. C lands on Venus. A’s orbiter reduces the cost to 2 energy. C gains the landing reward, first-landing data, and a yellow trace.
  7. A passes. A chooses 1 of the 3 remaining end-of-round cards.
  8. C passes. C chooses 1 of the final 2 cards and discards the other.

Round End

Everyone has passed, so round 1 ends:

  • each player gains 3 credits, 2 energy, and 1 card from starting income;
  • A and C each gain 1 additional credit; B gains 1 additional energy;
  • the starting-player marker passes to B;
  • the rotation reminder moves to the round 2 stack.

If a scan completes a sector, resolve that sector as soon as the Scan main action ends, before any later free actions.

13. Final Scoring

After the final player passes in round 5, score:

  1. points already earned;
  2. endgame cards with gold text boxes;
  3. gold milestones;
  4. additional scoring from revealed alien species.

Figure: Final scoring after round 5. Official Simplified Chinese rulebook, page 21, © Czech Games Edition; this site only makes the necessary local crop.

Each gold milestone tile has two sides:

Category One side Other side
Technology Each set of three different technologies Every two technology tiles
Missions Each completed mission Each pair of completed missions and/or endgame cards
Income Each set containing one credit, one energy, and one card income Whichever is more numerous: credit- or energy-income cards
Other Each pink-yellow-blue trace set; overflow counts Pair sector wins with orbiters + landers and take the lower number

The printed starting-income card does not count toward a gold income milestone. Repeated wins in the same sector count separately. Landers on moons also count.

Remaining credits, energy, publicity, ordinary cards, and data normally score nothing unless another rule refers to them. The highest score wins; tied players share the victory.

14. Space Agencies

The expansion has two layers:

  • Add directly to the base game: shuffle the 42 project cards into the base deck without replacing any cards; mix the 3 alien species with the base species; add the 10 signal tokens.
  • Use together as a module: 11 organizations and the quick start cards.

With only the first layer, play the normal 5 rounds. Organizations require quick starts and change the game to rounds 2–5, for 4 rounds total.

Organizations and Quick Starts

Figure: Eleven organizations with different starting resources and abilities. Official Space Agencies media assets, © Czech Games Edition; this site only trims transparent margins, resizes the image, and adds a neutral background.

When using organizations:

  1. Do not prepare round 1 or round 5 cards. Prepare stacks only for rounds 2, 3, and 4.
  2. Determine starting player and starting points normally. Everyone starts at 0 publicity.
  3. Deal each player 2 random organizations, 3 random quick starts, and 4 main-deck cards.
  4. Keep 1 organization, 2 quick starts, and all 4 hand cards.
  5. Everyone resolves both quick starts simultaneously, then gains the organization’s starting resources and effects.
  6. Begin round 2.

The upper half of a quick start places an orbiter, alien trace, or signal without gaining the location’s printed reward. The lower half grants starting resources, points, or another effect. Return the card to the box after resolution unless it explicitly becomes income.

Figure: Quick starts replace round 1 with one placement and one effect. Official Space Agencies media assets, © Czech Games Edition; this site only trims transparent margins, resizes the image, and adds a neutral background.

An organization may show:

  • starting resources;
  • a passive ability;
  • a once-per-round free action;
  • income increases that tuck cards.

Gain starting resources and quick-start rewards before tucking income. Resolve two income increases separately; a card drawn by the first may be tucked for the second.

Do not collect organization income at the start of round 2. Collect it only at the start of rounds 3, 4, and 5. This also resets once-per-round abilities. Organizations are balanced for four rounds; a five-round organization game is not recommended.

Further Context — Specialization and comparative advantage

Comparative advantage asks which output has the lower opportunity cost. An organization changes the cost or return of certain actions, while quick starts pre-place orbiters, signals, or traces. Evaluate the chain quick start → organization ability → main action → mission or milestone across one round; cards, species, and Solar System positions can still change the result.

For a first expansion game, use the official simplified setup. Use only organizations numbered 1–4; give each player 1 random organization, 2 quick starts, and 4 hand cards. Do not draft organizations or choose two of three quick starts.

In one- and two-player games, quick starts may be used without organizations. After players make their choices, reveal 4 random remaining quick starts. Resolve only their upper halves with an unused player color. Neutral signals act as one virtual player. With at most two signals, that player cannot win a sector, but it may take second place and leave a marker.

Solo setup still begins from the two-player rules. The rival receives no organization or quick starts, but:

  • shuffle the 4 new rival action cards into its deck;
  • start the rival at 4 publicity;
  • above the lowest difficulty, use the difficulty II and III objective deck;
  • add 2 random long-term objectives to the 3 difficulty II objectives, for 5 objectives total;
  • remove completed long-term objectives without replacement;
  • at the end of rounds 2, 3, and 4, each empty long-term-objective space advances the rival once; it adds no final-scoring penalty.

Signal Tokens

Figure: Gaining and using signal tokens, plus a counterexample. Official Simplified Chinese Space Agencies rulebook, page 8, © Czech Games Edition; this site only makes the necessary local crop.

Take 1 token from the common supply whenever an effect grants one. Tokens can be spent only during a Scan action:

  1. Discard any number of signal tokens.
  2. For each token, discard 1 additional card from the current card row.
  3. Choose one of that card’s two sector colors and mark a signal in a matching sector.

Refill the row after the entire scan. A basic scan already discards one of the three row cards, so normally at most 2 signal tokens can be used.

An effect that merely says “mark a signal” is not a Scan action and cannot spend signal tokens.

Three New Alien Species

Mix the 3 new boards with the 5 base-game species and choose 2 at random as usual. Discovery timing, contribution rewards, and overflow follow the base rules.

Spoiler-free summary:

  • Origin Ark gradually opens deeper research areas.
  • Glyphids ask the table to decode symbols together.
  • Amoeba rewards move around its board.
Reveal complete rules summaries for all three new species (mechanical spoilers)

Figure: Origin Ark, Glyphids, and Amoeba. Official Space Agencies media assets, © Czech Games Edition; this site only trims transparent margins and adds a neutral background.

Origin Ark

At discovery:

  1. Shuffle 9 exploration cards, set 4 aside at random, and build a deck from the remaining 5.
  2. Reveal 1 exploration card for each player marker in a discovery space. That player gains its minor reward, then discards the card.
  3. Each player takes 3 alert cards of different colors and places them trace-side up. With fewer than four players, return unused alerts without looking at them.

The Ark has alert levels 0–3. Everyone begins with access only to level 0. The first time you mark an Ark overflow area of a color, unlock your matching alert card and put it in your hand:

  • 1 unlocked card: access level 1;
  • 2 unlocked cards: access levels 1–2;
  • 3 unlocked cards: access every level.

Alert cards count toward the hand limit. Discard one for its free action to gain a minor exploration reward. Play one as a main action for 2 credits to gain a major reward. When the exploration deck runs out, shuffle all 9 cards, set aside 4, and rebuild the 5-card deck.

Glyphids

At discovery:

  1. Cover the species board with the decoding board and place both reward strips on random sides.
  2. Place random runes on the 6 species-board spaces, all 7 planets other than Earth, all 8 nearby stars, and every technology stack that still has its “first research +2 points” marker.

Take a rune when its condition is met. The conditions are: orbit or land at its planet or moon, win its sector, research its technology, or mark an alien trace on its species space. Refill the upper three species spaces at random from the reserve; other locations do not refill.

As a free action, place a rune you hold into an empty decoding space and gain its reward. An upper space requires both spaces below it to be filled. Each rune symbol can be decoded only once globally. A rune printed on a card grants its resource only after that symbol has been decoded; it does not grant a rune token.

At the end of the game, divide held runes into sets with no repeated symbol. Sets of 1–7 different runes score 1/3/5/8/11/15/20 points.

Some first-print reward strips show the same side twice. Use CGE’s official correction stickers; do not treat the misprint as a rules change.

Amoeba

At discovery:

  1. Shuffle 5 organelles and place them face up at random on the indicated spaces.
  2. Shuffle the 10 Amoeba cards.
  3. Give 1 card for each player marker in a discovery space, then reveal 1 face-up card for later acquisition.

Amoeba cards count toward the hand limit and may be tucked as income or discarded for their free action.

When marking an alien trace on the Amoeba board, gain the printed space reward and every organelle reward in that color region. Some Amoeba cards instead select 1 organelle reward in a specified region.

Each organelle that provided a reward then moves 1 space:

  • clockwise on the outer ring;
  • counterclockwise on the inner ring;
  • over occupied spaces to the next empty space.

If several organelles provided rewards, move all of them.

15. Four Official Promo Cards

Figure: The four promo cards published by CGE as of this revision. Official promo-card rules, © Czech Games Edition; this site crops one card from each rule page and arranges them without altering the cards.

Shuffle each promo directly into the main deck. The Space Agencies promo needs signal tokens and quick starts, so include it only when the expansion is available.

Not a Planet Since 2006 (Pluto)

After playing the card as a main action, keep it in front of you. Its illustration becomes your personal Pluto.

  • A probe in any space of the Solar System’s outer ring may use a later Orbit or Land action to move to the card.
  • Orbit costs 1 credit and 1 energy.
  • Land costs 3 energy, or 2 with your Pluto orbiter, and orange technology can reduce the cost.
  • The card holds only 1 orbiter and 1 lander, and only its owner may use them.
  • Pluto has no Solar System space, so visiting it cannot gain publicity.
  • Pluto still counts as a planet for other effects, missions, and gold milestones.
  • Cards #15 and #84 can remove its orbiter or lander; #16 may also allow another landing.

Gateway to Mars

Its two triggered-mission spaces may be marked by:

  • orbiting or landing at Mars, Phobos, or Deimos;
  • playing a card whose flavor text mentions “Mars” as a main action.

The qualifying base cards are #13, #14, #22, #34, #76, #84, #85, #119, and #ET.4. Space Agencies adds #31. If a card-granted landing action lands at Mars or one of its moons, the same event may mark both spaces.

Space Agencies

After playing it:

  1. Launch 1 probe for free.
  2. Gain 1 signal token.
  3. In the next game with organizations and quick starts, draw 1 extra quick start to choose from, but still keep only 2.

This effect carries between games. If the player group changes, seek everyone’s agreement before setup.

DLR

Launch for free, then gain a reward based on the sector aligned with Earth at the moment of launch:

  • yellow: 2 movement;
  • blue: 2 data;
  • red: 2 publicity;
  • black: 6 points.

Use Earth’s sector at launch, not the probe’s later destination.

The official upgraded components only replace the physical credits and energy; they add no rules. The Solar System randomizer generates a disc and sector layout and also adds no rules.

Recommended order:

  1. Learn the base game.
  2. Permanently add the 42 project cards, 3 species, and signal tokens.
  3. Enable organizations and quick starts together when you want asymmetric powers.
  4. Add promo cards as desired.

16. First-Game Reference

Setup Check

  • The three central boards are assembled.
  • Two alien-species boards are face down.
  • Eight sectors are clearly bounded and each star’s data slot is filled to its printed capacity.
  • The card row has 3 cards.
  • Gold milestones are on random sides and neutral milestone markers are correct.
  • All 12 technology stacks and first-research markers are ready.
  • Round 1–4 card stacks are ready.
  • Every player has the correct resources, publicity, hand, and tucked income.

Turn Check

  1. Free actions may be inserted before or during the main action; complete 1 main action each turn.
  2. Resolve completed sectors when the main action ends.
  3. Free actions may continue.
  4. At turn end, resolve milestones before alien discovery.

Common Errors

  • A newly launched probe may move during the same turn.
  • Leaving an asteroid costs extra movement; entering it does not.
  • An orbiter cannot become a lander. Any player’s orbiter reduces your landing cost.
  • Signals are mandatory. Excess signals still count for the majority.
  • Refill the card row only after the whole scan.
  • Sector ties go to the marker placed later.
  • The data pool holds 6. Analysis clears the computer, not the pool.
  • A free action may interrupt a main action but cannot interrupt another free action.
  • Increasing income grants the lower-right reward immediately.
  • Discard down to 4 cards only when passing.
  • Alien traces are mandatory, but overflow may be chosen.
  • Rotate before gaining every technology; the first player to pass also rotates.
  • Resolve milestones at turn end and before alien discovery.
  • Collect no income after round 5.
  • Ordinary leftover resources normally do not score. Tied players share the win.

Give the starting-player marker to the player who most recently saw a UFO and begin round 1.
entry.summary: Learn the SETI base game in play order: set up the table, understand turns and actions, resolve each checkpoint, and score the game; then add Space Agencies, its three alien species, and all four official promo cards.

entry.title: 《SETI》桌游规则：从摆桌到完成第一局

link.title: 《SETI》桌游规则：从摆桌到完成第一局

entry.content:
一、本文范围与阅读方式

本文先讲完整的《SETI》基础游戏，再单独讲《Space Agencies》和四张官方促销牌。扩展规则不会混入基础流程。

第一次学习时，建议按顺序阅读并同步摆放组件。已经玩过基础游戏的读者，可以直接进入扩展章节。三种新外星生物的详细规则收在折叠区内，默认不剧透。

正文中穿插八个“扩展理解”小栏，重点说明不同规则怎样接成行动链。外部知识只保留能帮助记忆的一层。它们不增加裁定规则；与规则书或牌面冲突时，以官方文本为准。

规则依据

  • 基础游戏：官方简体中文规则书与官方 FAQ。
  • 扩展：《Space Agencies》官方简中规则书与外星生物辅助页。
  • 促销牌：官方促销牌规则。
  • 单卡边缘情形：持续更新的官方卡牌澄清帖。

二、游戏目标与桌面概览

基础游戏进行 5 轮。终局总分最高者获胜；同分者并列获胜。

主要得分来源包括：

  • 打出项目牌和带金色文字框的终局牌；
  • 研发科技；
  • 赢得扇区；
  • 完成任务和里程碑；
  • 着陆、发现外星生物并继续研究。

图：一桌游戏的全景。SETI 官方媒体素材，© Czech Games Edition；本站仅缩放、压缩并铺设中性底色。

桌面分为四个区域：

  1. 中央太阳系：探测器从地球出发，在行星之间移动。
  2. 八个恒星扇区：玩家扫描信号、取得数据并争夺多数。
  3. 行星、科技和外星生物版图：分别处理着陆、升级和生命迹象。
  4. 玩家区：保存信用点、能量、手牌、探测器、数据和科技。

游戏中的生命迹象有三种：

  • 粉色：主要来自扫描和赢得扇区；
  • 黄色：主要来自行星着陆；
  • 蓝色：主要来自分析数据。

通用生命迹象带有三种颜色。获得时选择粉、黄、蓝中的一种处理。

扩展理解｜生命迹象与技术迹象

NASA 将生命留下的可观测证据称为生命迹象，将技术活动留下的证据称为技术迹象。游戏按行动来源分色：扫描与扇区连接粉色，着陆连接黄色，分析连接蓝色；这套分色用于串联规则，未模拟真实证据分类。

三、三人局设置

公共区

  1. 拼好行星版图、太阳系版图和科技版图。
  2. 洗混 5 块外星生物版图，背面朝上随机放 2 块。其余 3 块不看内容，收回盒中。
  3. 暂时不要取出物种专属卡牌、规则页和配件。物种揭晓后再取对应的一套。
  4. 随机组合三层太阳系圆盘和 4 块扇区版，形成 8 个边界清晰的扇区。每区对应一颗邻近恒星。
  5. 按板上印出的容量填满每颗恒星的数据槽。各恒星的槽位数不同。剩余数据、信用点和能量放在版图旁作为公共供应。
  6. 洗混主牌库，翻出 3 张组成卡牌供应区。
  7. 4 块金色里程碑各随机决定正反面。
  8. 选一种未使用的玩家颜色作为中立色，在分数轨 20、30 分位置各放 1 枚中立标记。
  9. 12 种科技各将 4 块板块洗混成堆，能力面朝下。每堆顶放 1 枚“首研＋2 分”标记。
  10. 为第 1–4 轮各准备 1 叠一轮结束牌。三人局每叠 4 张，即玩家数加 1。
  11. 一枚公转提醒标记放在科技版图的公转轨上，另一枚放在第 1 轮牌堆上。

玩家区

每位玩家：

  1. 选择颜色，拿对应的玩家版图、起始收入牌、8 个探测器、30 枚标记，以及分数和推广指示物。
  2. 按行动顺序从 1、2、3 分开始。最近看见 UFO 的玩家取得起始玩家标记。
  3. 将推广设为 4，拿 4 信用点、3 能量，再抽 5 张牌。
  4. 从手牌中选 1 张插到起始收入牌下，立即取得其右下角的信用点、能量或卡牌奖励。

插入信用点或能量收入牌后，手中剩 4 张牌。插入抽牌收入时会立即补抽，因此手中仍为 5 张。

图：玩家区包含三类科技、数据池、计算机、收入与资源轨。SETI 官方媒体素材，© Czech Games Edition；本站仅缩放、压缩并铺设中性底色。

其他人数

玩家数 20、30 分中立标记 每轮结束牌
2 人 每个位置 2 枚 每叠 3 张
3 人 每个位置 1 枚 每叠 4 张
4 人 不使用 每叠 5 张

四、回合结构与免费行动

一轮中，玩家按顺序反复获得回合。已经跳过的玩家不再参与本轮；其余玩家继续轮流行动，直到所有人都跳过。

一个回合按以下顺序进行：

  1. 主要行动前，可以先执行免费行动。
  2. 选择并完成 1 个主要行动；行动中也可以穿插免费行动。
  3. 主要行动结束时，立即结算该行动完成的所有扇区。多个扇区由当前玩家决定顺序。
  4. 扇区结算后，仍可继续执行免费行动。
  5. 结束回合：先结算里程碑，再处理外星生物发现。

图：七个主要行动与跳过本轮。官方简中规则书第 7 页，© Czech Games Edition；本站仅作必要局部裁切。

主要行动 基础费用与条件
发射探测器 2 信用点；放到地球
绕行行星 1 信用点＋1 能量；探测器已抵达该行星
在行星或卫星着陆 通常 3 能量；探测器已抵达目标
扫描邻近恒星 1 信用点＋2 能量
分析数据 1 能量；计算机上排 6 格已满
打出卡牌 支付白色效果区的费用
研发科技 6 推广；尚未拥有该科技
跳过本轮 无费用；本轮不再获得回合

常用免费行动：

  • 花 1 能量，让 1 个探测器移动 1 格；
  • 弃 1 张手牌，执行其左上角效果；
  • 将数据池中的 1 个数据放入计算机；
  • 支付两份同类资源，换取 1 信用点、1 能量或 1 张牌；
  • 花 3 推广，从卡牌供应区或牌库顶买 1 张牌；
  • 完成已经满足条件的卡牌任务；
  • 执行组件上标明的免费行动。

资源转换可以支付 2 张牌、2 信用点或 2 能量，不能混合支付。每移动一个数据、每移动探测器一格，都分别算一次免费行动。

免费行动只能在自己的回合使用。它可以插入主要行动，但不能用一个免费行动打断另一个免费行动。触发式任务是少数可以在其他玩家回合响应的效果。

效果原则上必须执行。只有移动和“增加收入”可以主动放弃。公转、信号、科技、资源、分数、生命迹象、牌面要求的主要行动和里程碑不能自行略过。若效果的一部分无法完成，只略过该部分。

五、探测器行动

图：同一种模型会成为探测器、人造卫星或着陆器；身份由所在版图决定。SETI 官方媒体素材，© Czech Games Edition；本站仅缩放与压缩。

发射与移动

发射探测器支付 2 信用点，将个人供应区的 1 个探测器放到地球。默认最多只能有 1 个探测器留在太空中。

发射后可以在同一回合移动。每花 1 能量，移动到一个正交相邻格：

  • 不能斜走；
  • 太阳不能进入或穿过；
  • 离开小行星格多花 1 点移动力，进入时不加价；
  • 进入带推广图标的天体，立即得 1 推广；地球除外；
  • 同一天体以后再次访问，仍可再次取得推广。

探测器可以停在太空中，等以后继续移动、绕行或着陆。

绕行

探测器抵达地球以外的行星后，可以在后续回合执行绕行：

  1. 支付 1 信用点和 1 能量。
  2. 将模型从太阳系移到该行星的轨道。
  3. 领取轨道奖励；该行星的第一位绕行者另得 3 分。

人造卫星不能继续移动，也不能改为着陆器。它不再占用“太空中探测器”上限。

着陆

探测器抵达目标后，可以在后续回合执行着陆：

  1. 通常支付 3 能量。
  2. 若该行星已有任意玩家的人造卫星，费用降为 2 能量。
  3. 将模型移到行星着陆区，领取分数、印刷奖励和黄色生命迹象。
  4. 第一位着陆者通常还能取得数据。

火星有两个数据位，前两位着陆者都能取得数据。

天然卫星着陆需要对应的探测器科技，或牌面明确允许。只领取卫星格上的奖励；是否获得黄色生命迹象也看该格图标。每个卫星格只能放 1 个着陆器。

着陆器不能移动，也不占“太空中探测器”上限。

扩展理解｜探测器任务链

一条完整链通常是“发射→免费移动→后续回合绕行或着陆”。发射可来自主要行动或卡牌；移动力可来自能量或卡牌；路线与费用还会受科技和已有卫星影响。读到牌面效果时，先确定它替代链条的哪一步，再补齐位置和费用条件。

六、扫描与扇区结算

扫描

扫描支付 1 信用点和 2 能量。基础扫描必须标记两个信号，以下两步顺序自定：

  1. 在地球当前对齐的扇区标记 1 个信号。
  2. 从卡牌供应区弃 1 张牌；从该牌右上角的两种颜色中选一个对应扇区，再标记 1 个信号。

等整次扫描及科技效果全部完成后，才将卡牌供应区补回 3 张。望远镜科技可以移动或增加信号；一次扫描最多可标记 4 个信号，并需支付科技写明的附加费用。

图：基础扫描的两个信号和望远镜科技。官方简中规则书第 12 页，© Czech Games Edition；本站仅作必要局部裁切。

标记信号

每次标记信号：

  1. 取走该扇区数据槽中最左边的数据，放入自己的数据池。
  2. 用自己的玩家标记填上刚空出的位置。
  3. 若填的是第二格，立即得 2 分。

标记信号是强制效果。数据槽已经填满玩家标记时，仍要将“超额信号”放在该槽旁。超额信号不给数据，但参与本次多数比较。

扇区结算

最后一个数据被替换时，该扇区完成。等当前主要行动结束后，按以下顺序结算：

  1. 标记最多者赢得扇区。平手时，较晚放下的标记获胜。
  2. 胜者在邻近恒星旁放 1 枚记录标记，并领取恒星奖励。
  3. 本次争夺中至少放过 1 枚信号的每位玩家得 1 推广；胜者也得。
  4. 用同样的数量与平手规则决定第二名。若存在第二名，其 1 枚标记留在重置后的第一格。
  5. 归还其他标记，重新用数据填满空位。

超额信号参与多数和参与资格；同一玩家每次结算仍只得 1 推广。恒星旁的既往胜利记录不参与下一次争夺。同一扇区可以多次完成和赢得。

图：扇区多数、奖励、第二名留标与重置。官方简中规则书第 13 页，© Czech Games Edition；本站仅作必要局部裁切。

扇区结算发生在主要行动结束时。若要在结算前放置数据、买牌或完成任务，必须把免费行动插入当前主要行动中。

七、数据与分析

取得的数据先进入数据池。数据池容量为 6；超过容量的数据必须弃置。

在自己的回合中，可以用免费行动将数据池中的 1 个数据放入计算机：

  • 基础计算机上排有 6 格，必须从左到右填；
  • 覆盖推广、增加收入或分数图标时，立即领取奖励；
  • 计算机科技增加上、下两格；
  • 只有对应上格已有数据，才能填下格；
  • 下格之间不要求从左到右。

上排 6 格填满后，可以支付 1 能量执行分析数据：

  1. 清除计算机上、下排的全部数据；
  2. 保留数据池中的数据；
  3. 标记 1 个蓝色生命迹象。

科技下格不需要填满，也不影响分析条件。

图：数据从数据池进入计算机；上排填满后才能分析。官方简中规则书第 14 页，© Czech Games Edition；本站仅作必要局部裁切。

扩展理解｜从候选信号到证据链

真实 SETI 会排除干扰并复测候选信号；Project Phoenix 还会调用第二台望远镜协助确认。游戏内的主链是“扫描→信号→数据池→计算机→分析→蓝色生命迹象”。若扫描填满扇区，先完成扫描及穿插其中的免费行动，主要行动结束时再结算扇区；数据池接近 6 时，应先检查能否装载或分析。

八、卡牌的四种用法

一张手牌只能选择一种用法：

  1. 打出：作为主要行动，支付白色区域的费用并执行效果。
  2. 弃置：作为免费行动，执行左上角效果。
  3. 增加收入：当效果允许时，插到起始收入牌下；立即取得右下角奖励，以后收入阶段重复取得。
  4. 资源转换：与另一张手牌一起支付，换取 1 信用点、1 能量或 1 张牌。

扩展理解｜机会成本

机会成本是选择一项用途时放弃的最佳替代方案。一张牌可以接入四条链：打出主要效果、弃牌执行免费行动、转为长期收入、与另一张牌换资源。若主要效果授予另一项行动，该行动免基础费用，但仍保留位置条件、科技附加费以及可能产生的任务、扇区和生命迹象结算。

图：项目牌实物特写。SETI 官方媒体素材，© Czech Games Edition；本站仅缩放与压缩。

图：卡牌左上是免费行动，左下是费用，白色区域是效果，右上是扇区颜色，右下是收入。官方简中规则书第 7 页，© Czech Games Edition；本站仅作必要局部裁切。

牌面若直接给出发射、扫描、绕行、着陆、分析或研发行动，不支付该行动的基础费用，但仍需满足位置等合法条件。若同时启用科技，仍要支付科技的附加费用。

任务分为两类：

  • 条件任务：在自己的任一回合，只要仍满足条件，就能作为免费行动完成。
  • 触发任务：只记录打出之后发生的事件。可以放弃一次触发，但以后必须重新发生符合条件的事件，不能追溯补标。

同一事件即使命中多个奖励圈，也只能选 1 个标记。带金色文字框的是终局牌；打出后保留，终局时计分。

从供应区取得卡牌后，通常立即补回 3 张。扫描是例外，需等整次扫描结束。主牌库抽空时，将弃牌堆洗成新的主牌库。

九、科技与太阳系公转

推广上限为 10。至少有 6 推广时，可以研发一种自己尚未拥有的科技：

  1. 支付 6 推广。
  2. 先执行太阳系公转。
  3. 从相应科技牌堆顶拿 1 块板块。
  4. 若这是该叠第一块被拿走的科技，移除“首研＋2 分”标记并得 2 分。
  5. 领取板块正面的一次性奖励，再翻面装到玩家版图。

图：探测器、望远镜和计算机科技。SETI 官方媒体素材，© Czech Games Edition；本站仅缩放与压缩。

  • 探测器科技：增加太空中的探测器上限、改善小行星移动、降低着陆费用或解锁天然卫星。
  • 望远镜科技：只在扫描行动中使用，改变或增加信号。
  • 计算机科技：增加数据格；上格通常提供 2 分，下格提供其他奖励。

太阳系按固定顺序公转：

  1. 第一次只转最上层；
  2. 第二次转中层，并带动上层；
  3. 第三次转底层，并带动上面两层；
  4. 第四次重新从最上层开始。

每次涉及的圆盘都逆时针转一个扇区。

图：太阳系公转的 1→2→3 循环。官方简中规则书第 16 页，© Czech Games Edition；本站仅作必要局部裁切。

扩展理解｜轨道力学与离散模型

开普勒第三定律说明轨道越远，周期通常越长；游戏只保留“相对位置会变化”，用 1→2→3 圆盘序列处理。研发链的顺序是“付推广→公转→处理探测器移动或推动→取得科技→领取奖励”，所以新科技来不及影响本次公转。首位跳过者触发同一套公转，并会改变仍在行动玩家的路线和地球朝向扇区。

公转由两类事件触发：

  • 玩家通过主要行动或卡牌取得科技；
  • 每轮第一位玩家跳过。

第 5 轮首位跳过者仍要公转。卡牌上与科技图标并列的公转符号只是提醒，不会额外公转一次。

圆盘之间露出的空位称为“缺口”。公转时按探测器所在位置处理：

  • 探测器在转动的圆盘上：随圆盘移动一个扇区；
  • 探测器在缺口中，圆盘没有碰到它：留在原位；
  • 转动的圆盘碰到缺口中的探测器：将它推到前方一格。

被推入带推广图标的天体时，其所有者立即取得推广，即使当前是其他玩家的回合。

十、跳过本轮与轮末

跳过也是主要行动。执行前可以先完成免费行动，然后按以下顺序处理：

  1. 手牌超过 4 张时，弃到 4 张。其他时候没有手牌上限。
  2. 若你是本轮第一位跳过者，执行一次太阳系公转。
  3. 第 1–4 轮，从本轮剩余的一轮结束牌中选 1 张加入手牌。

三人局中，首位跳过者从 4 张中选 1 张，第二位从 3 张中选 1 张，最后一位从 2 张中选 1 张并弃掉余牌。

完成跳过后，本轮不再获得回合，也不能再做免费行动。

图：弃到 4 张、首位跳过者公转、选择一轮结束牌。官方简中规则书第 19 页，© Czech Games Edition；本站仅作必要局部裁切。

第 1–4 轮全员跳过后：

  1. 每人领取起始收入牌上的 3 信用点、2 能量和 1 张牌。
  2. 再领取插在其下的全部收入。
  3. 起始玩家标记顺时针传给下一位。
  4. 公转提醒标记移到下一轮牌堆。

信用点、能量和手牌不会在轮末清零。第 5 轮没有一轮结束牌；最后一位玩家跳过后直接终局，不再领取收入。

扩展理解｜跳过连接本轮与下一轮

跳过链是“完成最后的免费行动→弃到 4 张→首位跳过者公转→第 1—4 轮选择一轮结束牌→等待全员跳过→领取收入”；第 5 轮在全员跳过后直接终局。首位跳过者会先改变太阳系，其他玩家继续在新布局上行动。跳过后无法再处理免费行动，因此可完成的卡牌任务、数据装载和资源转换都要提前完成。

十一、生命迹象、里程碑与外星发现

本节的“里程碑”指版图旁的金色里程碑板块，与卡牌任务分开处理。

放置生命迹象

获得生命迹象时必须放置对应颜色的标记。外星生物尚未揭晓时，可以选择：

  • 发现位：在任一物种下方的同色空位放标记，得 1 推广和 5 分。
  • 冗余区：在任一物种的同色冗余区放标记，得 3 分。

每个物种都有粉、黄、蓝各一个冗余区。冗余区不会填满，同色标记可以累积。即使仍有发现位空着，也可以主动选择冗余区。

图：三种生命迹象、发现位和外星生物揭晓流程。官方简中规则书第 20 页，© Czech Games Edition；本站仅作必要局部裁切。

回合结束时的里程碑

玩家首次达到或超过 25、50、70 分时，选择一块自己尚未选过的金色里程碑，将标记放在仍空着的最高分档。同一回合跨过多个门槛时逐一处理。这里只锁定终局计分位置，不立即取得里程碑分数。

三人局在 20、30 分各有 1 枚中立标记。首次达到或超过门槛的玩家，将该标记放入六个发现位中最左的空位：先填左侧物种的三格，再填右侧。中立标记不会进入冗余区或已揭晓的物种版图，但可能完成一次发现。

若同一回合有多位玩家达成里程碑，从当前玩家开始顺时针处理。所有中立标记放完后，再检查外星生物发现。

揭晓外星生物

一块物种下方的三个发现位填满时，在当前回合结束后揭晓：

  1. 先完成全部里程碑。
  2. 翻开物种版图。
  3. 取出该物种的规则页、卡牌和配件。
  4. 按规则页设置。
  5. 占据三个发现位的玩家领取该位置标出的“发现时”奖励。放置标记时已经取得的 5 分和 1 推广不重复领取。

冗余区中的标记不取得发现贡献奖励。

物种揭晓后，获得生命迹象时可以选择：

  • 已揭晓物种版图上的同色空位；
  • 尚未揭晓物种下方的同色发现位；
  • 任一物种的同色冗余区。

物种版图上的位置不要求从下向上填。放到哪里，就领取哪里的印刷奖励。

扩展理解｜外星发现汇合多条行动链

扫描与扇区、着陆、分析分别产生粉、黄、蓝标记；这些标记都可以进入同一组发现位。分数达到门槛时，中立里程碑标记也可能补上空位；所以一次只增加分数的行动，也可能在回合结束时促成发现。结束回合前，应同时检查分数门槛、发现位和处理顺序。

十二、一个完整的三人首轮

以下示例只使用确定的起始资源，不依赖行星或扇区的随机奖励。

前提：

  • A、B、C 依次行动，起始分数为 1、2、3。
  • 金星与地球正交相邻，中间不需离开小行星。
  • A、C 插入信用点收入牌；B 插入能量收入牌。
  • 设置后，A 与 C 各有 5 信用点、3 能量；B 有 4 信用点、4 能量。三人都有 4 张手牌和 4 推广。
  • 本例的扫描不会填满扇区。

行动记录

  1. A 发射并移动。 支付 2 信用点，将探测器放到地球；再用免费行动花 1 能量移动到金星，并取得 1 推广。A 剩 3 信用点、2 能量。
  2. B 扫描。 支付 1 信用点和 2 能量，标记地球扇区，再弃 1 张供应区卡牌标记第二个扇区。扫描结束后补牌。假设两个信号都取得数据，B 用两次免费行动将数据放入计算机第 1、2 格，并取得第 2 格的 1 推广。B 剩 3 信用点、2 能量。
  3. C 发射并移动。 过程与 A 相同。C 剩 3 信用点、2 能量。
  4. A 绕行金星。 支付 1 信用点和 1 能量，将探测器移到金星轨道，取得轨道奖励和首位绕行的 3 分。
  5. B 跳过。 手牌超过 4 张时先弃到 4 张；作为首位跳过者，执行公转；再从 4 张一轮结束牌中选 1 张。
  6. C 在金星着陆。 A 已有金星人造卫星，因此 C 只支付 2 能量。C 领取着陆奖励、首次着陆数据和黄色生命迹象。
  7. A 跳过。 从剩余 3 张一轮结束牌中选 1 张。
  8. C 跳过。 从最后 2 张中选 1 张，弃掉余牌。

轮末

三人都已跳过，第 1 轮结束：

  • 每人领取起始收入的 3 信用点、2 能量和 1 张牌；
  • A、C 各再领 1 信用点，B 再领 1 能量；
  • 起始玩家标记传给 B；
  • 公转提醒标记移到第 2 轮牌堆。

如果扫描填满扇区，应在该次扫描主要行动结束时先完成扇区结算，再继续后置免费行动。

十三、终局计分

第 5 轮最后一位玩家跳过后，按以下顺序计分：

  1. 已经取得的分数；
  2. 金色文字框终局牌；
  3. 金色里程碑；
  4. 已揭晓外星生物的额外计分。

十四、《Space Agencies》

扩展包含两类内容：

  • 直接加入基础游戏：将 42 张项目牌洗入基础牌库，不替换原牌；把 3 种外星生物与基础物种混合；加入 10 枚信号标记；
  • 成套启用：11 家研究机构和快速起始牌。

只加入第一类内容时，仍按基础游戏进行 5 轮。启用研究机构时，必须同时使用快速起始牌，游戏改为第 2–5 轮，共 4 轮。

研究机构与快速起始

图：十一家研究机构具有不同的起始资源和能力。《Space Agencies》官方媒体素材，© Czech Games Edition；本站仅裁去透明边缘、缩放并铺设中性底色。

使用研究机构时：

  1. 不准备第 1 轮和第 5 轮牌，只准备第 2、3、4 轮牌堆。
  2. 照常决定起始玩家与起始分数，所有玩家推广从 0 开始。
  3. 每人拿 2 张随机机构牌、3 张随机快速起始牌和 4 张主牌库卡牌。
  4. 保留 1 家机构、2 张快速起始和全部 4 张手牌。
  5. 大家同时结算两张快速起始，再领取机构的起始资源和效果。
  6. 直接开始第 2 轮。

快速起始牌上半部放置人造卫星、生命迹象或信号，但不取得所在位置原本的奖励。下半部提供起始资源、分数或其他效果。结算后收回盒中；牌面明确要求插入收入区时除外。

机构牌可能包含：

  • 起始资源；
  • 被动能力；
  • 每轮一次的免费行动；
  • 通过插牌增加的收入。

先领取起始资源与快速起始奖励，再插收入牌。连续获得两次“增加收入”时逐次处理；第一次抽到的牌可以用于第二次。

第 2 轮开局不领取机构收入。机构收入只在第 3、4、5 轮开始时领取；此时也重置“每轮一次”能力。不建议将机构模式延长为 5 轮。

扩展理解｜专业化与比较优势

比较优势关注哪类产出具有较低机会成本。机构能力会改变某些行动的成本或收益；快速起始又预先放置卫星、信号或生命迹象。评估机构时，沿“快速起始→机构能力→主要行动→任务或里程碑”计算一轮收益，牌序、物种和太阳系位置仍会改变结果。

首次使用时，可以采用官方简化设置。只用编号 1–4 的机构；每人随机取得 1 家机构、2 张快速起始和 4 张手牌，不进行二选一或三选二。

一至两人局可以单独使用快速起始。玩家选完后，从剩余牌中随机翻 4 张，只结算上半部，并用未使用的玩家颜色放置中立组件。中立信号视为一位虚拟玩家；它至多有两枚信号，不能赢得扇区，但可能取得第二名并留标。

单人模式仍按两人局设置。对手不取得机构或快速起始，但有以下调整：

  • 将 4 张新对手行动牌洗入对手牌库；
  • 对手以 4 推广开始；
  • 除最低难度外，使用难度 II、III 目标牌堆；
  • 另抽 2 块长期目标，与 3 个难度 II 目标组成 5 个目标；
  • 长期目标完成后移除，不补充；
  • 第 2、3、4 轮结束时，每个长期目标的空位让对手推进一次；终局不再追加惩罚。

取得信号标记时，从公共供应区拿 1 枚。它只能在扫描行动中使用：

起源方舟

发现时：

  1. 洗混 9 张探索牌，随机移出 4 张，以剩余 5 张组成牌库。
  2. 发现位上每有 1 枚玩家标记，就翻 1 张探索牌。该玩家取得次要奖励，然后弃牌。
  3. 每位玩家取得 3 张颜色各异的警戒牌，生命迹象面朝上。少于四人时，未使用的警戒牌不看内容直接收回。

方舟分为警戒等级 0–3。起初只能标记等级 0。在方舟某色冗余区首次放自己的标记时，解锁自己对应的警戒牌并拿入手中：

  • 解锁 1 张：可进入等级 1；
  • 解锁 2 张：可进入等级 1–2；
  • 解锁 3 张：可进入全部区域。

警戒牌计入手牌上限。弃牌执行免费行动，可取得次要探索奖励；作为主要行动支付 2 信用点打出，可取得主要奖励。探索牌库用完后，重新洗混全部 9 张，再移出 4 张并重建 5 张牌库。

符文族

发现时：

  1. 用破译版图覆盖物种版图，两块奖励板块各随机选择一面。
  2. 将符文随机放到物种版图 6 个位置、地球外的 7 颗行星、8 个邻近恒星，以及仍有“首研＋2 分”标记的科技堆。

满足对应条件时拿走符文。条件包括：在行星或其卫星绕行、着陆，赢得扇区，研发科技，或在带符文的物种位置标记生命迹象。物种版图上方三格拿走后从备用堆随机补充，其他位置不补。

可以用免费行动将持有的符文放入空的破译位，并领取奖励。上层位置要等下方两格填满；同一种符文全局只能破译一次。卡牌上的符文只在该符号已被破译后提供资源，不会给予符文标记。

终局时，将手中符文分成若干组，每组内符号不得重复。每组含 1–7 种符文时，分别得 1／3／5／8／11／15／20 分。

部分首批奖励板块正反面误印相同。应使用 CGE 的官方勘误贴纸，不要将误印视为规则变化。

阿米巴

发现时：

  1. 洗混 5 枚细胞器，正面朝上随机放到指定位置。
  2. 洗混 10 张阿米巴牌。
  3. 发现位上每有 1 枚玩家标记，该玩家取得 1 张牌；再翻 1 张正面朝上供后续取得。

阿米巴牌计入手牌上限，可以作为收入或弃牌免费行动使用。

在阿米巴版图标记生命迹象时，取得落点奖励和同色区域内所有细胞器奖励。部分阿米巴牌只让你选择指定区域内 1 个细胞器奖励。

真正提供过奖励的细胞器随后移动 1 格：

  • 外环顺时针；
  • 内环逆时针；
  • 前方被占时越过已占位置，落到下一个空位。

一次取得多个细胞器奖励时，每一枚都要移动。

十五、四张官方促销牌

图：截至本文修订时 CGE 公布的四张促销牌。官方促销牌规则页，© Czech Games Edition；本站从四页规则中各裁取牌面并排版，未改动牌面。

四张牌都直接洗入主牌库。Space Agencies 促销牌需要扩展中的信号标记和快速起始牌，因此只有扩展盒可用时才加入。

Not a Planet Since 2006（冥王星）

作为主要行动打出后，将牌留在面前。牌面视为你的个人冥王星。

  • 探测器位于太阳系最外环任一格时，可以用后续绕行或着陆行动移到牌上。
  • 绕行花 1 信用点和 1 能量。
  • 着陆花 3 能量；已有冥王星人造卫星时降为 2，并可受橙色科技减免。
  • 牌上限 1 颗人造卫星和 1 个着陆器，只有牌的拥有者可使用。
  • 冥王星没有太阳系格，不能通过访问取得推广。
  • 在其他效果、任务和金色里程碑中，冥王星仍算行星。
  • #15、#84 可以移除其人造卫星或着陆器；#16 也可能允许再次着陆。

Gateway to Mars

两格触发任务可分别由以下事件标记：

  • 在火星、火卫一或火卫二绕行或着陆；
  • 将背景文字提到 “Mars” 的牌作为主要行动打出。

符合的基础牌为 #13、#14、#22、#34、#76、#84、#85、#119、#ET.4；扩展另有 #31。若一张牌给出的着陆行动落在火星或其卫星，同一事件可以标记两格。

Space Agencies

打出后：

  1. 免费发射 1 个探测器；
  2. 取得 1 枚信号标记；
  3. 下一局使用机构和快速起始时，多抽 1 张快速起始牌供选择，但仍只保留 2 张。

这是跨局效果。下一局玩家有变化时，建议在设置前取得全体同意。

DLR

先免费发射，再按发射时地球对齐的扇区颜色取得奖励：

  • 黄色：2 移动力；
  • 蓝色：2 数据；
  • 红色：2 推广；
  • 黑色：6 分。

判断发射时的地球扇区，不看探测器随后移动到哪里。

官方升级组件只替换信用点和能量的材质，不改变规则。太阳系随机应用只生成圆盘和扇区组合，也不增加规则。

建议按以下顺序加入：

  1. 先玩基础游戏；
  2. 再常驻加入 42 张项目牌、3 种外星生物和信号标记；
  3. 需要不对称能力时，同时启用机构与快速起始；
  4. 按需加入促销牌。

十六、首局速查

设置核对

  • 中央三块主版图已拼好；
  • 2 块外星生物版图背面朝上；
  • 8 个扇区边界清楚，恒星数据槽已按印刷容量填满；
  • 卡牌供应区有 3 张牌；
  • 金色里程碑已随机翻面，中立里程碑数量正确；
  • 12 叠科技和首研标记已放好；
  • 第 1–4 轮牌堆已准备；
  • 每位玩家的资源、推广、手牌和收入牌已设置。

回合核对

  1. 主要行动前或进行中可穿插免费行动；每回合完成 1 个主要行动。
  2. 主要行动结束时结算完成的扇区。
  3. 可以继续做免费行动。
  4. 回合结束时先处理里程碑，再处理外星生物发现。

常见误读

  • 发射后可以在同一回合移动。
  • 离开小行星才增加移动费用。
  • 人造卫星不能改为着陆器；其他玩家的人造卫星也能降低你的着陆费用。
  • 标记信号是强制的；超额信号仍参与多数。
  • 扫描结束后才补充供应区。
  • 扇区平手时，较晚放下的标记获胜。
  • 数据池上限 6；分析清空计算机，不清数据池。
  • 免费行动可以插入主要行动，不能互相嵌套。
  • 增加收入时立即取得右下角奖励一次。
  • 手牌只在跳过时弃到 4 张。
  • 生命迹象必须放置，但可以选择冗余区。
  • 每次取得科技都先公转；每轮首位跳过者也公转。
  • 里程碑在回合结束时处理，并先于外星生物发现。
  • 第 5 轮结束后不领取收入。
  • 剩余普通资源通常不计分；同分者并列获胜。

将起始玩家标记交给最近看见 UFO 的玩家，从第 1 轮开始。
entry.summary: 按实际游玩顺序讲清《SETI》基础游戏：先摆桌，再掌握回合、行动、结算与终局；后附《Space Agencies》、三种新外星生物及四张官方促销牌。

entry.title: Quantifying Resource and Point Values in Age of Innovation

link.title: Quantifying Resource and Point Values in Age of Innovation

entry.content:
Preface

Age of Innovation: A Terra Mystica Game is a standalone game set in the Terra Mystica world. In terms of mechanisms familiar to players, it can also be understood as a substantial reworking of Terra Mystica. Its development flow has much in common with Gaia Project, so the approach to quantifying resources can be carried across the two games.

Resource values keep iterating from round to round while also being affected by staged rewards, action windows, and player interaction. They are difficult to describe precisely with a single formula. This article attempts to convert different resources onto an approximate common scale and then compare their practical value during a game. Unless a statement is explicitly identified as an official rule, terms such as “profitable,” “unprofitable,” and the relative rankings below refer to the results under this article’s valuation framework, not fixed prices supplied by the game.

**Source note Positioning of the game**

The official Feuerland Spiele page defines it as a standalone game in the Terra Mystica world. The official Capstone Games rulebook lists the buildings, resources, ability tiles, and Book actions discussed in this article.

Notation

This article retains the older abbreviations I used for Terra Mystica and Gaia Project. In this game, they correspond to:

  • Buildings: M = Workshop, TC = Guild, RL = School, AC = University, and SH = Palace.
  • Resources: C = Coins, O = Tools, B = Books, P = Scholars (the original draft also called them priests), and K = spaces on the Science display (called the cult track in the original draft).
  • Rounds: T1 means round 1, T6 means round 6, and so on.

Because literal formulas must stay identical across the bilingual pair, their Chinese labels are retained: 资源 means resources, 分 means points, 魔 means Power, 产 means income, 铲 means Spades, 航 means Shipping, and 桥 means Bridges. Each formula’s surrounding English text also states its interpretation.

Converting Resources

Coins and Tools: C & O

Using the exchange ratio of Power actions, this article counts each Coin as 1 point of general-purpose resources and each Tool as 3 points:

1c = 1 点通用资源
1o = 3 点通用资源

This is only the baseline unit used for the comparisons that follow.

Science Display: K

Returns from the Science display are relatively direct: 12k can bring 8 Power and 8 points; reaching 9k can produce 3c or 3 points; and each space on the display also brings a one-time return of roughly 1–1.5 resources in the corresponding round.

If reaching 9k in T4 and taking 3 points is used as the reference, the approximation can be written as:

1k = 1.5 资源 + 1.4 分

In English, the retained formula values 1k as 1.5 resources plus 1.4 points.

Books: B

Books derive their value mainly from two uses.

Innovations

Innovations—the original draft called them “advanced tiles”—are the main outlet for Books. Taking an Innovation worth roughly 18 points for 5, 6, or 7 Books gives the coarse estimate:

1b = 3.6 分

That is, one Book is approximated as 3.6 points.

Book Actions

Surplus Books can be spent on Book actions. The official rules provide the following actions; any Coins or points to the right of the equals signs are valuations from this article’s model:

  • 1b = 5 魔 = 2.5c
  • 1b = 2k = 3c + 2.8 分
  • 2b = 6c, so 1b = 3c
  • 2b = 3c2o = 9c, so 1b = 4.5c
  • 2b = 2/4/6/8 分, so 1b = 1–4 分
  • 3b = 3 铲; because the Spades are normally used early, this can be valued as 1b = 3o = 9c

The actions most likely to produce a positive return are:

  1. 3b = 3 铲, so 1b = 9c
  2. 1b = 2k, so 1b = 3c + 2.8 分
  3. 2b = 升级 TC, so 1b = 4.5c

Considering all these uses together, each Book can be valued at 5 points of general-purpose resources. This does not conflict with the valuations of particular Book actions above: 1b = 5 魔 is only the fallback exchange. When free Spades or progress on the Science display can be used fully, a Book’s practical return can be much higher. In particular, 3b = 3 铲 has very high practical value when all the free Spades can be used.

Late in the game, once the conditions for converting 6b into points are in place, breaking those 6b apart for ordinary Book actions is almost always a loss under this article’s framework.

**Source note Book actions**

Page 23 of the official English rulebook lists six Book actions: exchange 1 Book for 5 Power; advance 2 spaces on the Science display for 1 Book; take 6 Coins for 2 Books; upgrade a Workshop to a Guild for free for 2 Books; score 2 points per Guild for 2 Books; and perform Terraform and Build with 3 free Spades for 3 Books.

Scholars: P

Combining Power conversion with the types of buildings that produce them, each Scholar is valued roughly at 5 points of general-purpose resources.

Scholars also have two broad uses.

Science Display

Sending a Scholar can advance 3/2/1k, corresponding to:

p = 4.5/3/1.5 资源 + 4.2/2.8/1.4 分

The three alternatives respectively provide 4.5, 3, or 1.5 resources plus 4.2, 2.8, or 1.4 points.

Early in the game, Scholars can therefore be paired with round rewards to contest the 3k space, while the 2k space is better left for later. When the advance gained by sacrificing a Scholar is used as the valuation basis, each k can alternatively be counted as 2 resources.

Upgrading Shipping and Terraforming

Shipping and Terraforming primarily act as functional hard thresholds that must be unlocked at specific times. Their value is difficult to express accurately in resources alone, so these upgrades should first serve the overall development plan for the game.

Baseline Position

Starting Resources

This article selects one concrete starting setup as its baseline:

  • Faction: using the Goblins, 12c + 1o + 2k = 19
  • Terrain: using Wasteland, 15c + 4o + 2b = 37
  • General starting resources: 2m + 2o + 4 魔力, equivalent under this framework to 2×5 + 2×3 + 4×0.5 = 18 (each of the two starting Workshops is valued at 5 resources, and each Power at 0.5)
  • Per-round income: 1o + 特权片 6c = 9

The first three static components total 74. After including the 9 resources produced at the start of T1, the model uses 83 resources as the starting point of the first round’s Action phase, followed by another 9 resources of income in each subsequent round.

Endgame Resources

The following endgame position serves as the valuation target:

9m 2tc 3rl sh ac 3航 3铲 4p 3桥 24k

In this retained notation, 航 means Shipping upgrades, 铲 means Spades, and 桥 means Bridges.

Expanded on the common scale used here:

9×5  2×14  3×28  32  23  3×9  3×13  4×5  3×3  24×2

The total is 355 resources.

Endgame Score

At the time, I used the game performance of high-scoring player Sertuy as a reference and treated 205 points as an experiential anchor for a player who develops reasonably and contests first place. This number serves the approximate model below; it is not a fixed winning threshold for every player count, map, and setup.

Iterative Resource Conversion Rate

The model approximately maps 83 resources in T1, plus 9 resources of continuing income in each round, through five cross-round conversions into 355 resources and 205 points in T6.

Let each point of resources become x resource points after one round of iteration while also producing y points. The resource side satisfies:

\[83x^5 + 9(x^4 + x^3 + x^2 + x + 1) = 355\]

Solving gives the iterative resource conversion rate:

\[x \approx 1.27\]

Within this experiential model, I further take:

\[y \approx 0.19\]

Each resource point therefore iterates approximately into 1.27 资源 + 0.19 分 per round. One resource in T1 can become 3.3 resources and 1.62 points by T6, making the cross-round value of early resources quite substantial.

Round T1 T2 T3 T4 T5 T6
Resources 1 1.27 1.61 2.04 2.60 3.30
Points 0 0.19 0.43 0.74 1.12 1.62

Under the same model, the endgame resources and net points from charging Power can be written as:

Round T1 T2 T3 T4 T5 T6
Charge 1 1.65+0.81 1.30+0.56 1.02+0.37 0.81+0.21 0.63+0.10 0.5+0
Charge 2 3.30+0.62 2.60+0.12 2.04-0.26 1.61-0.57    
Charge 3 4.95+0.43 3.90-0.32 3.06-0.89 2.42-1.35    
Charge 4 6.60+0.24 5.20-0.76 4.08-1.52      

The table uses the endgame fallback conversion of 5 general-purpose resources for 1 point. The official rule “5 Coins = 1 point” is likewise only a poor endgame conversion and does not represent a resource’s practical value during the game. As long as buildings, ability tiles, Book actions, or round-scoring windows remain available, resources can usually achieve a higher conversion rate.

To estimate the practical value of converting resources into points during the game, this article uses a T6 opportunity that can still convert 2o3c into 3 points. With 1o = 3c, this is equivalent to 3c = 1 分, which gives:

T1 的 1c ≈ T6 的 2.72 分

In English: one Coin in T1 is approximately equivalent to 2.72 points in T6.

This is not an official endgame conversion rule. It is the marginal value used by this article to compare opportunities during the game.

The resulting general rule for charging Power is to upgrade high-value buildings near other players whenever possible before T3, then take smaller Power charges after T3. This is one way to improve resource returns.

Comparing Returns from Buildings

With a common resource scale and cross-round conversion relationship, the resource conversion rates of different buildings can be compared. Equivalent costs, equivalent outputs, and conversion rates in the table all follow the framework above.

Base building M TC RL AC SH
Base cost 2c1o 3c2o 5c3o-3k 8c5o-3k 6c4o
Equivalent cost 5 9 14-6 23-6 18
Resource output 1o 2.5~3c 1p+1o1k 10+1o1k+5c 4 Power+1o1k
Equivalent output 3 2.5 10 20 7
Upgrade conversion rate 0.60 -0.06 0.54 0.43 0.25
Conversion rate when upgrading from M - -0.06 0.30 0.37 0.15

Under this valuation, building inexpensive M and RL early is profitable; AC can be built when an Innovation is needed. TC is a severe loss early in the game.

Large buildings are important to the endgame structure, so they should still be considered at an appropriate time even when their immediate conversion rates are not high.

Spades

Cost to expand with M 1o 2o 3o
Equivalent cost 8 11 14
Upgrade conversion rate 0.38 0.27 0.21

Under this model, even expanding with an M that requires only 2o has a lower resource conversion rate than building an AC.

Strength Analysis

Ability Tiles

In general, choosing resource production in T1 and T2, then gradually shifting toward points from T3 onward, produces relatively high returns under this model. Actual expansion can be constrained by terrain, distance, and Action-phase timing, so resource balance and expansion planning must still be considered together.

2c and 3-Point Income

Use 2c + 3 分 as the baseline for comparisons among ability tiles.

1o1k Income

1o1k = 4.5c + 1.4 分

That is, the 1o1k income is valued as 4.5c plus 1.4 points.

Compared with 2c3 分产, the break-even round for 2.5c = 1.6 分 lies approximately in T3–T4. This gives:

T1：1o1k 产 ≥ 2c3 分产
T1 之后：2c3 分产 > 1o1k 产

In English: 1o1k income is at least as valuable as 2c plus 3-point income in T1; after T1, the 2c plus 3-point income is more valuable.

1b and 1-Power Income

1b1 魔 = 5.5c

That is, the income of 1b plus 1 Power is valued as 5.5c.

Compared with 1o1k 产, the break-even round for 1c = 1.4 分 lies approximately in T3. This gives:

T1：1b1 魔产 ≥ 1o1k 产
T1 之后：1o1k 产 > 1b1 魔产

In English: 1b plus 1-Power income is at least as valuable as 1o1k income in T1; after T1, 1o1k income is more valuable.

4-Power Action

4 魔 = 2c，并附带当回合产出 2c

The retained line says that 4 Power equals 2c and also produces another 2c in the same round.

Under this article’s framework, it is strictly weaker than 1o1k 产 and is suitable only when Power must be replenished or an additional synergy can be created.

Double Spade

即时 6o = 18c，T1 终局价值 = 59.47c + 29.18 分
即时 4o = 12c，T1 终局价值 = 39.65c + 19.60 分
T1 1o1k 产的终局价值 = 38.40c + 18.19 分
T1 1b1 魔产的终局价值 = 46.93c + 13.67 分

In English, the four lines give the T1 endgame values of an immediate 6o as 59.47c plus 29.18 points, an immediate 4o as 39.65c plus 19.60 points, 1o1k income as 38.40c plus 18.19 points, and 1b plus 1-Power income as 46.93c plus 13.67 points.

Double Spade theoretically gains a few more points, but using 4o to terraform two spaces in succession is not usually urgent early in the game. Its practical advantage over persistent-production tiles is therefore not as large as the numbers suggest.

Summary

Among resource-producing ability tiles, the T1 ranking is:

1b1 魔产 ≥ 1o1k 产 ≥ 2c3 分产

That is, in T1, 1b plus 1-Power income ranks at least as high as 1o1k income, which in turn ranks at least as high as 2c plus 3-point income.

Double Spade is also an option, and the differences among these ability tiles in T1 are small. After T1, only 2c3 分产 should normally receive priority.

Tools, the Science display, Books, and Power all have strongly stage-dependent values, so the final choice must still serve the development plan for the whole game.

**Source note Ability tiles and round scoring**

Page 24 of the official English rulebook lists the ability tiles and round-scoring tiles compared here. The rules specify only the resources and points they provide; their relative strength in different rounds is an analytical result of this article’s model.

Book Actions

1b = 5 Power

3 分 = 2.5c can generally be exchanged in T1–T3 and becomes a slight loss after T4.

1b = 2k

3 分 = 3c + 2.8 分. As long as enough Books remain to acquire an Innovation, this is a good choice in any round.

2b = 6c

3 分 = 3c can generally be exchanged in T1–T4 and becomes a slight loss after T5.

2b = Upgrade TC

3 分 = 4.5c can generally be exchanged in T1–T4 and becomes a slight loss after T5.

2b = Points per TC

3 分 = 1–4 分; consider it when there are at least three TCs.

3b = 3 Spades

Early in the game, this can be valued as 1b = 3o = 9c and is highly profitable. Late in the game, it can instead be approximated as 3 分 = 1o = 3c, becoming a slight loss after T5.

Faction

Moles

The analysis below preserves the Mole faction board and valuation framework used by the original draft:

1o = 2 分 can easily become a point-scoring trap. If only direct point conversion is considered, 3c = 2 分 does not become profitable until after T5.

The early-game Moles can therefore be treated essentially as having 1 Shipping. Their faction ability usually scores fewer than 10 points even late in the game, and its value is more functional than numerical.

A more advantageous use is to concentrate a large wave of Workshops in a single round when an M round-scoring tile appears in T5 or T6, paired with the M-scoring ability tile. The early game can accordingly focus on compact expansion through RL while also maintaining Tool income.

**Version note Moles**

In September 2024, Feuerland Spiele released an official faction adjustment, which was incorporated beginning with v1.2. In the revised Moles, the jumping score became 2 + X, where X is the number of other players. This section therefore preserves historical analysis under the old-version model and should not be treated directly as a current v1.2 faction guide.

Conclusion

The purpose of this quantitative method is to place Coins, Tools, Books, Scholars, Science spaces, and action opportunities temporarily on one scale, making it easier to compare several candidate plans within a game. Its clearest implication is that resources obtained earlier, and put into development promptly, have more opportunities to keep appreciating over subsequent rounds.

Actual games still include staged rewards, map position, player interaction, and functional thresholds, so decisions should not be made mechanically from the tables alone. The numbers here are better suited to checking whether a development plan is broadly reasonable than to prescribing a single building or ability-tile order across factions and maps.
entry.summary: This article attempts to convert the different resources in Age of Innovation onto a common scale and uses a cross-round iterative model to compare their practical value during a game.

entry.title: 《大创造时代》资源-分值量化计算思路

link.title: 《大创造时代》资源-分值量化计算思路

entry.content:
前言

《大创造时代》（Age of Innovation: A Terra Mystica Game）是 Terra Mystica 世界中的独立作品。若从玩家熟悉的机制来理解，也可以把它看作对《神秘大地》的一次大幅改造；它和《盖亚计划》的发展流程有不少相似之处，因此资源量化的思路也可以互相借鉴。

资源的价值会在轮次之间不断迭代，同时受到阶段性收益、行动窗口和玩家互动的影响，很难用一套公式精确描述。本文尝试把不同资源换算到一个近似的通用尺度，再据此比较它们在局中的实际价值。除非明确写作官方规则，下文的“赚”“亏”和强弱排序都指本文估值口径下的结果，不是游戏给出的固定定价。

资料说明｜游戏定位

Feuerland Spiele 官方页面将本作定义为 Terra Mystica 世界中的独立游戏；Capstone Games 官方规则书列出了本文涉及的建筑、资源、能力板和书行动。

记号

本文沿用我在《神秘大地》和《盖亚计划》中的旧缩写。它们在本作中分别对应：

  • 建筑：M = Workshop，TC = Guild，RL = School，AC = University，SH = Palace。
  • 资源：C = 金币，O = 工具，B = 书，P = 学者（Scholar，原稿也称祭司），K = 科学轨道格（Science display，原稿称信仰轨）。
  • 轮次：T1 表示第 1 轮，T6 表示第 6 轮，以此类推。

资源换算

金币和工具 C & O

本文按魔力行动的兑换关系，将每个金币记为 1 点通用资源，每个工具记为 3 点通用资源，即：

1c = 1 点通用资源
1o = 3 点通用资源

这只是后续比较所采用的基准单位。

科学轨道 K

科学轨道的收益相对直接：12k 可带来 8 魔力和 8 分；到达 9k 后有 3c 或 3 分的产出；每个轨道格还会在相应轮次带来约 1–1.5 点资源的一次性收益。

若按 T4 到达 9k 并取得 3 分计算，合计可近似写成：

1k = 1.5 资源 + 1.4 分

书 B

书的价值主要来自两个方向。

创新

创新（Innovation，原稿称“高级片”）是书的主要消耗渠道。若以 5/6/7 本书取得一个约值 18 分的创新作为基准，可以粗略取：

1b = 3.6 分

书行动

多余的书可以用于书行动。官方规则给出的行动数量如下；等号右侧的金币或分值换算是本文模型中的估值：

  • 1b = 5 魔 = 2.5c
  • 1b = 2k = 3c + 2.8 分
  • 2b = 6c，即 1b = 3c
  • 2b = 3c2o = 9c，即 1b = 4.5c
  • 2b = 2/4/6/8 分，即 1b = 1–4 分
  • 3b = 3 铲；铲通常用于前期，因此可计 1b = 3o = 9c

其中，比较容易产生正收益的行动有：

  1. 3b = 3 铲，即 1b = 9c
  2. 1b = 2k，即 1b = 3c + 2.8 分
  3. 2b = 升级 TC，即 1b = 4.5c

综合各项用途，每本书可以记为 5 点通用资源，与上面对具体书行动的估值并不冲突：1b = 5 魔只是保底兑换，在能够充分利用免费铲子或推进科学轨的局面下，书的实际收益可以明显更高。尤其在能够充分利用免费铲子的情况下，3b = 3 铲有很高的实际价值。

到了后期，如果已经具备 6b 换分的条件，再拆掉 6b 去做普通书行动，按本文口径几乎必亏。

资料说明｜书行动

官方英文规则书第 23 页列出的六种书行动分别是：1 本书换 5 魔力、1 本书前进 2 个科学轨道格、2 本书换 6 金币、2 本书免费把 Workshop 升为 Guild、2 本书按 Guild 数量每座得 2 分，以及 3 本书执行一次带 3 个免费铲子的 Terraform and Build。

学者 P

综合魔力转换和生产建筑的类型，每个学者粗略记为 5 点通用资源。

学者的用途也可以分为两类。

科学轨道

派出学者可以前进 3/2/1k，对应：

p = 4.5/3/1.5 资源 + 4.2/2.8/1.4 分

因此，前期可以配合回合奖励争取 3k 格；2k 格则更适合留到后期。若按牺牲学者换取轨道推进的口径计算，每个 k 也可以记为 2 点资源。

航海和掘地升级

航海与掘地更多承担功能性的硬门槛，需要在特定时间解锁，很难只用资源量准确表示。这类升级首先应服从整局的发展规划。

基准盘面

开局资源

本文选择一组具体开局作为基准：

  • 种族：以哥布林计算，12c + 1o + 2k = 19
  • 地形：以 Wasteland 计算，15c + 4o + 2b = 37
  • 通用起始资源：2m + 2o + 4 魔力，按本文口径折合 2×5 + 2×3 + 4×0.5 = 18（2 座开局 Workshop 各记 5 点资源，魔力每点记 0.5）
  • 每回合产出：1o + 特权片 6c = 9

前三项静态资源合计 74；计入 T1 的首轮产出 9 后，模型以 83 点资源作为第一轮行动阶段的起点，之后每轮继续产出 9 点资源。

终局资源

本文取以下终局盘面作为估值目标：

9m 2tc 3rl sh ac 3航 3铲 4p 3桥 24k

按本文的统一尺度展开：

9×5  2×14  3×28  32  23  3×9  3×13  4×5  3×3  24×2

合计 355 点资源。

终局分数

我当时参考了高分玩家 Sertuy 的对局表现，把 205 分作为玩家合理展开并争取第一名时的经验锚点。这个数字服务于下文的近似模型，不表示所有人数、地图和配置下的固定胜分线。

资源迭代转换率

模型把 T1 的 83 点资源和每轮 9 点持续产出，经过五次跨轮转换，近似映射到 T6 的 355 点资源与 205 分。

设每点资源每轮迭代后变为 x 点资源，并同时产生 y 分。资源侧满足：

\[83x^5 + 9(x^4 + x^3 + x^2 + x + 1) = 355\]

解得资源迭代转换率：

\[x \approx 1.27\]

在这套经验模型中，进一步取：

\[y \approx 0.19\]

因此，每点资源每轮近似迭代为 1.27 资源 + 0.19 分。T1 的 1 点资源到 T6 可以转化为 3.3 点资源与 1.62 分，前期资源的跨轮价值相当可观。

轮数 T1 T2 T3 T4 T5 T6
资源 1 1.27 1.61 2.04 2.60 3.30
分值 0 0.19 0.43 0.74 1.12 1.62

按照同一模型，吸魔的终局资源与净分值可以写成：

轮数 T1 T2 T3 T4 T5 T6
吸1 1.65+0.81 1.30+0.56 1.02+0.37 0.81+0.21 0.63+0.10 0.5+0
吸2 3.30+0.62 2.60+0.12 2.04-0.26 1.61-0.57    
吸3 4.95+0.43 3.90-0.32 3.06-0.89 2.42-1.35    
吸4 6.60+0.24 5.20-0.76 4.08-1.52      

表中把 5 点通用资源换 1 分作为终局清仓的保底口径。官方规则中的“5 金币 = 1 分”也只是一种亏损的终局兑换，并不代表资源在局中的实际价值；只要仍有建筑、能力板、书行动或回合计分窗口，资源通常可以实现更高的转化率。

为了估计局中资源换分的实际价值，本文采用 T6 仍能以 2o3c 完成一项 3 分转化的情形。按 1o = 3c 计算，这相当于 3c = 1 分；由此可得：

T1 的 1c ≈ T6 的 2.72 分

这不是官方的终局兑换规则，而是本文用于比较局中机会的边际价值。

由此可以得到吸魔的一般规律：T3 前尽可能在人堆里升级较高建筑，T3 后再蹭取小额魔力，是提高资源收益的一种思路。

各建筑收益对比

有了统一的资源尺度和跨轮转换关系，就可以比较不同建筑的资源转换率。表中的等值消耗、等值产出和转换比均沿用前文口径。

基础建筑 M TC RL AC SH
基础消耗 2c1o 3c2o 5c3o-3k 8c5o-3k 6c4o
等值消耗 5 9 14-6 23-6 18
资源产出 1o 2.5~3c 1p+1o1k 10+1o1k+5c 4魔+1o1k
等值产出 3 2.5 10 20 7
升级资源转换比 0.60 -0.06 0.54 0.43 0.25
从 M 升级转换比 - -0.06 0.30 0.37 0.15

按这套估值，前期建造便宜的 M 和 RL 是赚钱的；需要取得创新时可以建 AC。TC 在前期血亏。

大建筑对终局结构比较重要，因此即使即时转换率不高，在时机合适时仍应考虑建造。

铲子

扩 M 花费 1o 2o 3o
等值消耗 8 11 14
升级资源转换比 0.38 0.27 0.21

按本文模型，即使扩张一个 M 只需要 2o，资源转换率仍然不如建造 AC。

强弱分析

能力板

总体而言，T1、T2 选择资源产能、T3 以后逐渐转向得分，是这套模型下收益较高的节奏。实际扩张会被地形、距离和行动阶段卡住，因此仍要同时考虑资源平衡与扩张规划。

2c3 分产

把 2c + 3 分作为能力板之间的基础比较项。

1o1k 产

1o1k = 4.5c + 1.4 分

与 2c3 分产比较，寻找 2.5c = 1.6 分的临界回合，大致位于 T3–T4。由此判断：

T1：1o1k 产 ≥ 2c3 分产
T1 之后：2c3 分产 > 1o1k 产

1b1 魔产

1b1 魔 = 5.5c

与 1o1k 产比较，寻找 1c = 1.4 分的临界回合，大致位于 T3。由此判断：

T1：1b1 魔产 ≥ 1o1k 产
T1 之后：1o1k 产 > 1b1 魔产

4 魔行动

4 魔 = 2c，并附带当回合产出 2c

按本文口径，它严格弱于 1o1k 产，只适合必须补充魔力或能形成额外配合的局面。

双铲

即时 6o = 18c，T1 终局价值 = 59.47c + 29.18 分
即时 4o = 12c，T1 终局价值 = 39.65c + 19.60 分
T1 1o1k 产的终局价值 = 38.40c + 18.19 分
T1 1b1 魔产的终局价值 = 46.93c + 13.67 分

双铲在理论上多赚几分，但前期通常并不急需用 4o 连续铲两块地，因此和持续产能板的实际差距没有数字看上去那么大。

小结

在资源产出能力板中，T1 的排序为：

1b1 魔产 ≥ 1o1k 产 ≥ 2c3 分产

双铲也可以选择，几种能力板在 T1 的差距不大；T1 之后则只建议优先考虑 2c3 分产。

工具、科学轨、书和魔力都有很强的阶段性，最终选择仍应服务于整局的发展规划。

资料说明｜能力板与回合计分

官方英文规则书第 24 页列出了本文比较的能力板及回合计分板。规则只规定它们提供的资源和分数；不同轮次的强弱关系属于本文模型的分析结果。

书行动

1b = 5 魔

3 分 = 2.5c，大致在 T1–T3 可以兑换，T4 以后略亏。

1b = 2k

3 分 = 3c + 2.8 分。只要书仍足够取得创新，任何轮次都是不错的选择。

2b = 6c

3 分 = 3c，大致在 T1–T4 可以兑换，T5 以后略亏。

2b = 升级 TC

3 分 = 4.5c，大致在 T1–T4 可以兑换，T5 以后略亏。

2b = TC 数量分

3 分 = 1–4 分；当 TC 数量不少于 3 时可以考虑。

3b = 3 铲

前期可按 1b = 3o = 9c估值，非常赚钱；后期则可近似视为 3 分 = 1o = 3c，T5 以后略亏。

种族

鼹鼠

以下分析保留原稿所依据的鼹鼠派系板和当时的估值口径：

1o = 2 分容易成为刷分陷阱；若只考虑纯刷分，3c = 2 分要到 T5 以后才开始赚钱。

因此，前期的鼹鼠基本可以看作 1 航海；后期的种族技能通常也刷不到 10 分，价值更多体现在功能性。

比较有优势的用法，是在 T5、T6 出现 M 回合计分板时，配合 M 计分能力板在单轮集中爆铺。相应地，前期可以 RL 缩地为主，并兼顾工具产能。

版本说明｜鼹鼠

Feuerland Spiele 在 2024 年 9 月发布了官方派系调整，并从 v1.2 起纳入新版。新版鼹鼠的跳跃得分改为 2 + X，其中 X 为其他玩家人数。因此，本节保留的是旧版模型下的历史分析，不应直接当作当前 v1.2 的种族攻略。

结语

这套量化方法的作用，是把金币、工具、书、学者、科学轨和行动机会暂时放到同一尺度上，帮助判断一局之内的几个候选方案。它最能说明的是：越早获得、并且能够及时投入发展的资源，越有机会在后续轮次继续增值。

实际对局仍然包含阶段性奖励、地图位置、玩家互动和功能性门槛，不能只按表格机械决策。本文的数字更适合用来检查发展计划是否大致合理，而不是跨派系、跨地图给出唯一的建筑或能力板顺序。
